text.p: German qualifier Martin Sinner claimed the scalp of world number 17 Tim Henman in the first round of the $1 million Dubai Open on Monday.
Some erratic ground strokes that often overshot the baseline cost the the British number one dear as he went down 7-6 6-4.
Sinner played way above his 183rd world ranking and it was his ability to play big points that frustrated Henman.

"I think today luck was by my side," said Sinner. "I had more patience and played much better top spin which was good for me and hard for him. The victory has given me enough confidence to get back into the top 100."

Henman started off well, keeping up the pressure with steady play from the baseline. He came close to breaking Sinner seven times in the first set but all too often failed to control his sliced backhands.
In the tiebreak Sinner was fully charged up, often stranding Henman with stinging cross-court volleys. He raced to a 6-2 lead and went on to win the tiebreak 7-5.
A Henman double fault gave Sinner a break in the third game of the second but he lost his own service the following game.
With Henman failing to find the right mix of strokes, Sinner, ranked 46th in 1995, broke again in the ninth game and went on to hold his service to win the set and match.
"I am pretty disappointed to lose in the first round but then Martin deserved to win. He played much better," said Henman.
"I created some chances in the first set but just couldn't capitalise on them."
Earlier, Argentina's Hernan Gumy overcame Australian James Sekulov 6-4 6-3. Playing mostly from the baseline. Gumy was too steady for his less experienced opponent.
